fixes.explanation: A throne would be a nice touch, friend, but the verse doesn't have one. It says many were appalled at Him because His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man (Isaiah 52:14). Later the people speaking say He had "…no stately form or majesty to attract us…" (Isaiah 53:2). That's the picture the text gives.

Crowds coming to see His face isn't in the verse, friend. It says He had "…no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him." (Isaiah 53:2). Nothing in His looks pulled people in.

That's it, baker. The verse says "Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not." He was treated like someone men hide their faces from (Isaiah 53:3). I think that's the heavy part.

Children don't show up in this verse, friend. The text says "Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised…" He was treated like someone men hide their faces from (Isaiah 53:3). It's about faces.

Kings do show up in Isaiah 52:15, friend, where they shut their mouths because of Him. But in 53:5 the text says "…the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him…" The Servant is the one who "…was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities…" (Isaiah 53:5). The punishment landed on Him.

It really does say that, friend. The verse says "…by His stripes we are healed." The people speaking say it about themselves, right after saying He was pierced and crushed (Isaiah 53:5). His stripes come first, and the healing is theirs.

A ram in a thicket is a fine picture, friend, but it's from another story (Genesis 22:13). In Isaiah 53:7 the pictures are a lamb and a sheep. "He was led like a lamb to the slaughter…" That's the animal for this verse.
No fighting here, friend. The verse says "…He had done no violence…" (Isaiah 53:9). And another verse says He did not open His mouth (Isaiah 53:7). Nothing in the passage shows Him fighting back.

Look at the very last line, friend. It says "Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors." Intercession means speaking up on someone's behalf. So He was numbered with the transgressors, and He also spoke up for them (Isaiah 53:12).
